name: Ultimate Downloadable Products for WooCommerce
author: ethereumicoio

sections.description:
Ultimate Downloadable Products for WooCommerce plugin allows to display downloadable files on a product page.

This plugin is ideal to sell digital products to show customers what they will get after a purchase.

It can be a valuable addition to your NFT selling store with the NFT WordPress Plugin Kit!

FREE Features

  • Option to show a Downloads tab with downloads list on the product page
  • Shortcode [ultimate-downloadable-list] to display downloadable files on a product page (with no ability to download)
  • Option to show image thumbnails for downloads of type image
  • File type icon, file size and file count in the list
  • Scheduled downloads: unlock N days after purchase, set in WooCommerce’s own Downloads block on the product
  • Until then the My Account downloads list shows “Available in N days” as text instead of a link, the product page says when the files unlock, and a refused download explains itself without using up the customer’s download
  • An unlock email when a scheduled file opens — a WooCommerce email under WooCommerce → Settings → Emails, switchable in the plugin settings
  • Download protection: direct requests to wp-content/uploads/woocommerce_uploads/ are blocked on Apache-compatible servers, the rule is re-verified once a day, and the settings screen says whether it is in force — with the exact snippet to paste when the plugin is not allowed to write it

PRO Features

The PRO version includes all FREE features, plus:

  • Option to specify the thumbnail width for downloads of type image
  • Option to show blurred thumbnails for downloads of type image
  • Option to specify the thumbnails blur strength for downloads of type image
  • Per product preview settings: width, blur and strength, each of them inherited from the plugin options until the product overrides it
  • Per file preview settings: a different width, blur or strength for one download
  • Per product Downloads tab setting: show or hide the tab on a product without changing the global option
  • Variable Downloadable products support
  • Archive file contents display
  • Audio sample: a download of type audio plays a short generated clip (30 seconds by default) in the list, from its own file rather than from the product file
  • Video sample: a download of type video shows a blurred poster and plays a short clip in a modal window
  • Document preview: the first page of a PDF is shown as an image, or its opening lines as a text excerpt when the server has no page renderer
  • RAR and ISO archive type upload support
  • Scheduled & drip release — files unlock N days after purchase, or on a date you choose; Professional adds a separate schedule per file. Until then the shop does not hand out a working download link, and the plugin blocks direct access to your downloads folder on Apache-compatible servers and shows you exactly what to paste on the others. This is access control plus server-side file protection — not encryption: a file that was already downloaded stays downloaded.
  • An unlock date for one customer: the order screen and wp udp schedule unlock|status override a single permission without touching the product
  • Subscription-aware schedules: a file stays locked while the WooCommerce Subscription is not active, and a renewal never restarts the schedule

Roadmap

The functionality planned in next versions:

  • WCFM frontend feature compatibility
  • Dokan frontend feature compatibility
  • WCVendors PRO frontend feature compatibility

sections.installation:
• Install and activate it as you would any other plugin.
  • Make a new WooCommerce downloadable product.
sections.faq:
What is the shortcode?

[ultimate-downloadable-list] prints the download list of the product being displayed. The Downloads tab renders the same list, so the tab and the shortcode never disagree.

Does it work with variable products?

Yes, in the PRO version: each downloadable variation is listed under its own name.

Does this stop a customer from downloading before the date?

Yes, for the shop’s own download link. Until the unlock instant WooCommerce’s download URL answers 403 with a page that says when the file opens and links back to My Account, and the My Account list shows “Available in N days” as text instead of a link. A refused attempt costs the customer nothing: it does not consume a download, does not appear in the download log, does not change the remaining count, and a media or range request (Range: bytes=...) is refused the same way instead of being served in slices. What the plugin controls is the link WooCommerce hands out — the file itself is the next question.

Can a customer download a file before the date?

Not through the shop; and on a protected server, not by copying the file URL either. The plugin writes a rule that blocks direct requests to wp-content/uploads/woocommerce_uploads/, checks once a day that the rule really works, and shows the result on its settings screen. On servers that ignore .htaccess (nginx, most CDNs) the plugin cannot write the rule: it shows you the exact snippet to paste and keeps a warning in your dashboard until the check passes. Use “Force downloads” rather than “Redirect only” — the redirect method hands the file URL to the browser by design, so no rule can protect it. This is not encryption: a file that was already downloaded stays downloaded.

Why did the unlock email arrive late?

The unlock email is a WP-Cron event scheduled for the unlock instant, and WP-Cron runs when somebody visits the site. If DISABLE_WP_CRON is set in wp-config.php and no system cron calls wp-cron.php, the event stays pending in the cron option — it is late, never lost, and it goes out with the next cron run whenever that happens. So that a waiting customer is not made to wait for a cron run, the same check also runs on the My Account downloads page: the mail leaves the first time the customer looks there, at most once an hour per site. Two switches have to be on: “Email the customer when a download unlocks” in the plugin settings, and the “Download ready” email in WooCommerce → Settings → Emails. Turn either off and the schedule still works, silently.

Do I need WooCommerce Subscriptions?

Only for the subscription-aware lock, which is a Professional feature. Without WooCommerce Subscriptions the plugin never looks at subscriptions and a schedule counts from the order. With it, a file stays locked while the subscription is on hold, cancelled or expired, and a renewal does not restart the schedule: the delay counts from the subscription’s start, not from the last payment. Verified against WooCommerce Subscriptions 7.6.0.

Why are my image thumbnails missing?

The GD PHP module is required to generate them. The settings screen ends with a Server capabilities report, and wp udp status prints the same matrix from WP-CLI — both are the first thing to check.

What do the audio, video and document previews need?

Audio samples need both the ffmpeg and the ffprobe commands, and video samples need them too; without both, audio and video downloads keep the file type icon, the file size and the file count. Document page images need poppler-utils (the pdftoppm command) or the Imagick PHP extension built with its PDF delegate; when only pdftotext is available the download shows a text excerpt instead of an image. Documents are PDF only — DOCX, ODT and other office formats keep the file type icon row, because rendering them would need a separate office suite on the server.

The samples are also bounded on purpose: the file must be stored under wp-content (a remote download is never sampled), and a source shorter than the sample length plus ten seconds is never sampled, because the sample would be the product. Generation runs in the background, so a freshly saved product may show icons until WP-Cron catches up; wp udp previews media generates the samples from WP-CLI, and the product panel’s readiness line says how many are still pending. The settings screen and wp udp status report which of these tools this server actually has.

What are the requirements?

PHP 8.1 or newer, WordPress 6.0 or newer, WooCommerce 7.0 or newer. Thumbnails need the GD module, the RAR and ISO formats need the matching PHP modules (see below). Audio, video and document previews need extra command line tools — see the preview question above.

Why does the plugin need to write a file to my uploads folder?

Because the link is not the only way to a file. WooCommerce keeps downloads in wp-content/uploads/woocommerce_uploads/, which your web server serves without PHP — no plugin hook is in that path, so a copied URL would work no matter what the schedule says. On an Apache-compatible server (Apache, LiteSpeed) the plugin therefore adds its own marked block to the .htaccess in that folder, adds an index.php there when the folder has none, and on uninstall removes exactly its own block. Lines it did not write are never touched: a php_value directive or a hotlink rule your host put there survives verbatim. Files stored on a remote host or a CDN are not in that folder and are not covered.

What if my server is nginx?

nginx ignores .htaccess, and the plugin does not write server configuration it does not own. The settings screen shows the exact snippet for nginx — location ^~ /wp-content/uploads/woocommerce_uploads/ { deny all; }, or internal; when you use X-Sendfile / X-Accel-Redirect — plus the Caddy and the IIS web.config versions, and it keeps a warning in your dashboard until the check passes. After saving the snippet, reload the web server and press “Check again”.

Why is the warning still there after I added the rule?

Because the plugin believes a measurement, not the file it wrote. Once a day — and every time you press “Check again” — it puts a small temporary .txt file into the downloads folder and requests it over HTTP. 403 or 404 means protected; a 200 or a redirect means a browser can still fetch the file; a timeout, a 401 or a server error means it could not verify, and “could not verify” is never shown as protected. So if the warning survives, one of three things is true: the web server was not reloaded, it is not reading that file, or the site cannot reach itself over HTTP. The same state is written to the WooCommerce log and printed by wp udp status.

Are the downloads protected behind a CDN?

Partly, and the plugin says so where it matters. The rule protects the origin folder. A copy a CDN has already cached keeps being served from the CDN’s own URL until that cache is purged — the rule cannot purge it. A file stored on a remote host (a CDN URL in the product’s download row) was never in the uploads folder, so no rule on your server applies to it at all; the settings screen names such a file when your shop has one.

How to configure server to support RAR, 7z or ISO?

Follow recommendations from this guide please.

Contact the PRO version support for help.
sections.changelog:
3.1.0

  • New: scheduled downloads – a product’s files unlock a number of days after purchase, set in WooCommerce’s own Downloads block on the product
  • New: until a file unlocks, My Account shows “Available in N days” instead of a link, the product page says when the files unlock, and a refused download explains itself and uses up nothing
  • New: an unlock email when a scheduled file opens – a “Download ready” WooCommerce email under WooCommerce → Settings → Emails, switchable in the plugin settings
  • New (PRO): unlock on a fixed date, a separate schedule per file, and an unlock date for one order on the order screen and from wp udp schedule unlock|status
  • New (PRO): subscription-aware schedules – files stay locked while the WooCommerce Subscription is not active, and a renewal does not restart the schedule
  • New: download protection – the plugin blocks direct requests to the downloads folder on Apache-compatible servers, re-checks once a day that the rule really works, and shows the state, the last check and the exact nginx / Caddy / IIS snippet on the settings screen
  • New: a dashboard warning on every admin screen while downloads are not protected – it can be postponed for 7 days and comes back, and the settings row stays red until the check passes
  • New: wp udp status prints the protection state, and the product panel warns the merchant when a file unlocks after its downloads expire

3.0.0

  • New: audio downloads can play a short sample right in the downloads list
  • New: video downloads show a blurred poster and play a short sample in a modal window
  • New: PDF downloads show their first page as an image, or their opening lines as a text excerpt when no page renderer is available
  • New: a per product Media preview choice and a per file Preview column in the Downloads preview panel, with a Samples ready line for the samples still being generated
  • New: the settings screen and wp udp status tell you whether this server can make the samples, and wp udp previews media generates them from WP-CLI
  • Samples are generated in the background – a product save never starts one – and every sample is a short excerpt, never the product file
  • Samples need ffmpeg and ffprobe (audio and video) or poppler / Imagick with the PDF delegate (documents); without them every download keeps its icon, size and count

2.2.0

  • New: per product preview settings – thumbnail width, blur and blur strength can be set on a single product and inherit the plugin options by default
  • New: per file overrides – one download can use its own width, blur or strength
  • New: the Downloads tab can be shown or hidden per product
  • The product data panel gains a Downloads preview tab with all of the above

2.1.0

  • New: file type icons, file sizes and a file count in the downloads list
  • Thumbnails are generated when a product is saved and served as files from the uploads directory, instead of being generated on the first visit and inlined as base64 in the product meta
  • New: wp udp previews regenerate fills the previews of an existing catalogue
  • The thumbnail cache now includes the download id, so two downloads of one product can point at the same file

2.0.0

  • Restructured into layered modules (the plugin behaves exactly as 1.3.5; this release moves code)
  • Requires PHP 8.1, WordPress 6.0 and WooCommerce 7.0
  • New: wp udp status prints the plugin version, the settings and the server capabilities
  • New: the settings screen ends with a server capability report (GD, ZipArchive, RAR, ISO, ffmpeg)

1.3.5

  • freemius library version update
  • tested up to WordPress 7.1 and WooCommerce 11.2

1.3.4

  • freemius library version update

1.3.3

  • freemius library version update

1.3.2

  • freemius library version update

1.3.1

  • freemius library version update

1.3.0

  • Option to show image thumbnails for downloads of type image released in a free plugin version

1.2.0

  • Zip and other archive types content display added
  • RAR and ISO archive type upload support

1.1.0

  • Variable Downloadable products support

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
